title: Conditions of Cover: the Free-Look Period on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
Only the policyholder may give up their own Travel Protection Plans cover, and the cancellation is confirmed by the policyholder rather than performed on their behalf.

A free-look cancellation is handled at the full refund only when frozen time is not after the moment the certificate of insurance was issued to the policyholder plus the free-look period of the plan held. The period runs from the moment of issue recorded against the certificate, which is the system's own record of when the certificate of insurance was issued, and not from what the policyholder recalls of it.

The free-look period is counted in whole calendar days from the day after the issue date, weekends and public holidays included, and a cancellation confirmed exactly on the closing day is still inside the period.

Inside the free-look period the whole premium is returned to the original form of payment, the policy fee excepted, and the agency's commission is recovered in full.

The free-look right is lost as soon as the journey has begun or a claim has been filed, whichever comes first, however many days of the period remain.

Outside the free-look period the mid-term terms apply instead, and the two are never combined.

A returned premium is raised against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as several refund lines.

## The condition set out as a test

| What must hold | What decides it |
| --- | --- |
| The policyholder is the one giving up the cover | The cancellation is confirmed by the policyholder |
| The moment is not after issue plus the plan's free-look period | The moment of issue recorded against the certificate, plus that plan's period in whole calendar days |
| The journey has not begun | The certificate's own dates for the journey insured |
| No claim has been filed | The claim record of that certificate |

## Both sides of the closing day

Counting begins on the day after the issue date. On a plan whose free-look period is 10 calendar days, a certificate issued on a given day has its closing day on the tenth day after that day.

Inside the period: a cancellation confirmed on that closing day is inside the period, because the comparison is not-after and the boundary day itself satisfies it. The whole premium is returned, the policy fee excepted, and the commission is recovered in full.

Outside the period: a cancellation confirmed on the day following that closing day is after the moment of issue plus the plan's period, so the free-look refund is not handled, and the mid-term terms apply in its place.

Lost before the period runs: where the journey has begun, or a claim has already been filed on the certificate, the free-look right is gone on the day it happened, whatever the calendar would otherwise allow.
